response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders o JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) > '2013-10-25 17:40:25' AND CAST(o.date_order_placed AS TEXT) < '2017-05-24 19:26:44' GROUP BY c.gender) SELECT gender, order_count, order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM g) AS above_average FROM g WHERE order_count > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM g)

assumptions.assumption: Customers with NULL gender form their own group (one group, counted in the average) because GROUP BY keeps NULLs as a group; the inner join keeps only orders whose customer exists.
The average is the unweighted mean of per-gender order counts across all gender groups present in the filtered data, as the request states.
